assessment: The paper provides a complete quantitative framework for spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) in a 2D BEC via the Kibble-Zurek mechanism. It includes a numeric control (quench time tau_Q), numeric readouts (vortex number n_v, equilibration time t_eq, incompressible and compressible kinetic energy spectra E_i(k), E_c(k), total energies E_i, E_c, structure functions S_p(r)), and quantitative mechanisms (KZ scaling laws, Kolmogorov scaling, universal collapse). The source supports multiple fitted power-law relations with coefficients and exponents, enabling an interactive experiment. Case authoring is ready.

mechanisms.statement: The incompressible kinetic energy spectrum E_i(k) exhibits Kolmogorov scaling E_i(k) ∝ k^{-5/3} in the inertial range, and a k^{-3} scaling at higher momenta due to vortex core structure. Fits for τ_Q=100 and τ_Q=350 yield exponents α ≈ 1.71 and 1.65 for the inertial range, and β ≈ 3.03 for the high-k range.

mechanisms.statement: The longitudinal velocity structure functions S_p(r) exhibit extended self-similarity, with S_p(r) ∝ [S_3(r)]^{ζ(p)}. Fitted exponents for τ_Q=350 deviate from K41 prediction ζ(p)=p/3 and are described by K62 with κ=0.114±0.006.

paper_scope: The paper uses numerical simulations of the 2D stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii equation to study the formation of a newborn BEC via a thermal quench of the chemical potential, focusing on the emergence of spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) and its characterization through Kibble-Zurek scaling of vortex number and Kolmogorov scaling of the incompressible kinetic energy spectrum. It establishes universal collapse of energy spectra under KZ rescaling and analyzes compressible energy, structure functions, and enstrophy evolution.

source_ambiguities.statement: The main text defines t_eq as the equilibration time measured from the crossing of the critical point, while the supplementary material defines t_eq as t_2 from the second derivative criterion. The main text fit omits the linear term that appears in the supplementary fit.
